R-launch-2.ownerDecision: Approved: the wait between accounts may end early when the previous client's log reports that it joined (the evidence registry's Connected/joined evidence). O-C9-1.kind: minor finding from round 3's independent lane review (verify it first; the reviewer can be wrong)
O-C9-1.title: A row held for an update uses a stand-in count of one running client for as long as the process inventory is untrusted, including when desktop.Problem is set or ProcessInventoryComplete stays false fo
O-C9-1.problem: A row held for an update uses a stand-in count of one running client for as long as the process inventory is untrusted, including when desktop.Problem is set or ProcessInventoryComplete stays false for a long time. If the monitor keeps failing after every Roblox client has closed, the row still shows ClientUpdateHold.Explanation ("This request starts on its own once no Roblox client is running"). That is now false: no client is running, the row still cannot start, and what actually blocks it is the missing fresh process evidence. The fixer documented this tradeoff, and starts stay refused in every case, so safety is not affected.
O-C9-1.proposedFix: Keep the hold only through a short run of untrusted samples, for example while the last fresh sample is younger than about 2x MaximumEvidenceAge or the monitor's sample interval. Alternatively, keep the stand-in only when desktop.Problem is null. Either way, a long monitoring failure falls back to the "fresh complete process evidence is required" explanation. Add a test in which a held row sees persistently untrusted samples well past that window.

O-C11-1.title: Once an owner stalls, UseAsync abandons it, but its workers keep running
O-C11-1.location: src/Zenith.Sessions.App/SelfCheckOwners.cs:30-35 together with src/Zenith.Sessions.App/DistributionSelfCheck.cs:122-123 (using var vault/repository/cleanup/settings) and :319 (using setupProjection); src/Zenith.Sessions.Windows/ProtectedCredentialVault.cs:901 and AccountIdentityProjection.cs:310
O-C11-1.problem: Once an owner stalls, UseAsync abandons it, but its workers keep running. Meanwhile the stage-scoped `using` resources they still use are disposed as the try block unwinds. ProtectedCredentialVault.Dispose and AccountIdentityProjection.Dispose throw InvalidOperationException ("Cancel and await pending ... before disposal") while a call is still active. That new exception replaces the tagged TimeoutException before `catch(Exception ex)` sees it. Example: NativeHandoffCoordinator dispatches through `_vault.TryDispatchCurrentAsync(finalGrant, () => start)`. If the token-less start stalls (the exact case N-B10-3 targets), the report reads ErrorType=InvalidOperationException, FailingMethod=Zenith.Sessions.Windows.ProtectedCredentialVault.Dispose, CauseType=null. It does not name NativeHandoffCoordinator.DisposeAsync, and the deadline cause is gone. The same happens in "Direct verified account creation" when setupService stalls inside a projection call. The report is still written and the run still exits 1, so this only mislabels the failure. But it contradicts the claim that the report names the stalled owner, and no test stalls a vault- or projection-holding owner.
O-C11-1.proposedFix: Record the stage failure before the stage's shared `using` resources unwind. For example, move the repository/vault/cleanup/settings declarations outside the try. Or wrap the stage body in an inner try that builds FailedCase from the first exception and keeps it when a later Dispose throws. Then add a test that stalls the starter inside NativeHandoffCoordinator.DispatchAsync (or a projection call) and asserts that FailingMethod is the stalled owner's DisposeAsync.

O-C11-2.kind: minor finding from round 3's independent lane review (verify it first; the reviewer can be wrong)
O-C11-2.title: The filter runs after WaitAsync has already timed out
O-C11-2.problem: The filter runs after WaitAsync has already timed out. If the owner finishes in the gap between the bound expiring and the filter running, the filter is false and WaitAsync's raw, untagged TimeoutException escapes. The stage's own failure (for example the deadline OperationCanceledException or an InvalidDataException from the work) is lost, StalledOwner returns null, and FailedCase points FailingMethod at framework await code. The window is narrow, but a borderline-slow shutdown lands in exactly this case.
O-C11-2.proposedFix: Decide from a single observation. For example, `var finished = await Task.WhenAny(shutdown, Task.Delay(bound)) == shutdown;`, then throw the tagged timeout if not finished, otherwise `await shutdown` and rethrow `failure`. Or, inside the catch, when `shutdown.IsCompleted`, observe shutdown and rethrow `failure` instead of letting the WaitAsync timeout escape.

O-C11-3.kind: minor finding from round 3's independent lane review (verify it first; the reviewer can be wrong)
O-C11-3.title: The allowlist says ManagerDiagnostics "waits at most 3 s for its writer and then cancels it"
O-C11-3.problem: The allowlist says ManagerDiagnostics "waits at most 3 s for its writer and then cancels it". In fact, after the 3 s StopAsync does `_stop.Cancel(); await _writer`, which has no bound. A writer blocked in its synchronous File.Move/FileInfo/FileStream open ignores the token, so this stage can still hold the report. The stage disposes it through an explicit `await diagnostics.DisposeAsync()` (line 574), and the guard regex only inspects `await using`, so explicit DisposeAsync awaits are never checked (PackagedLayoutCheck.cs:146 is another). The timing comment "15 s deadline plus this bound stays inside the 20 s" also ignores two costs: this 3 s wait, and two healthy-but-slow nested owners after the deadline, which can each use nearly the full 2 s. That is about 19 s plus process start-up against the script's 20 s WaitForExit, which also covers start-up.
O-C11-3.proposedFix: Route the diagnostics stage through SelfCheckOwners.UseAsync, and bound the explicit inner DisposeAsync with the same helper or WaitAsync(bound). Extend the guard to flag `await <x>.DisposeAsync()` in self-check files. Reword the budget comment to state the real worst case (one bound per nested owner that is healthy but slow, plus the 3 s diagnostics wait), or shorten the bound for nested owners.

O-C8-1.kind: minor finding from round 3's independent lane review (verify it first; the reviewer can be wrong)
O-C8-1.title: OwnerOf decides same-tracker launches by time, but the new cross-tracker exclusivity check ignores time completely
O-C8-1.problem: OwnerOf decides same-tracker launches by time, but the new cross-tracker exclusivity check ignores time completely. Suppose launch L1's log was created before launch L2 began, and the log also names L2's tracker (for example the websiteBTId plus the 'BTID is overriden to' pair the head reader accepts). L1 is then marked Ambiguous even though L2 cannot own that log. LaunchLogExpectation.From offers up to 32 receipts, old terminal ones included, so this false Ambiguous can last as long as both receipts stay in the window. The row then reads 'more than one log or launch shares this browser tracker', which is not what happened: no other log or launch shares L1's tracker; L1's log names another launch's tracker. The direction is conservative (it never produces a wrong Linked), and the fixer stated the tradeoff, but the UI text misdescribes the case this change made more common.
O-C8-1.proposedFix: In the exclusivity loop, skip other launches whose NotBeforeUtcTicks is later than head.CreatedUtcTicks, because they cannot own the log. Also reword the Ambiguous text so it covers 'this launch's client log also names another launch's tracker', or add a separate status or reason. Pin the change with a test variant of ALogThatAlsoNamesAnotherLaunchsTrackerLinksNeitherEvenWhenThatLaunchCannotLink in which the second launch begins after the log was created.

O-C8-2.kind: minor finding from round 3's independent lane review (verify it first; the reviewer can be wrong)
O-C8-2.title: There is a documented race
O-C8-2.problem: There is a documented race. An earlier same-tracker launch's client may create its log only after the relaunch began (slow bootstrapper update) while the relaunch itself produces no log. That log is then credited to the relaunch, whose row reads 'Client log: names this launch's browser tracker · held by PID <the earlier launch's client>', and the earlier launch shows NotLinked. The old rule made both rows Ambiguous. The link stays corroboration only (CanAuthorizeAccountAction false), but the user sees the wrong PID on a launch row. The tradeoff is recorded only in a code comment. The ledger and QUALITY_STATUS do not mention it.
O-C8-2.proposedFix: Record the tradeoff next to the N-B7-1 row and the launch-to-log notes (HANDOFF.md:47 or the ledger) when the merge step updates QUALITY_STATUS, so the owner can keep or reverse it. Optionally, in that window, add a qualifier to the Linked text such as 'an earlier launch with the same tracker has no log yet'.

O-C6-1.kind: minor finding from round 3's independent lane review (verify it first; the reviewer can be wrong)
O-C6-1.title: N-B5b-6 is only partly closed
O-C6-1.problem: N-B5b-6 is only partly closed. A seen key is kept only if it is already in _soundSeenClients. Suppose one of the user's own clients is unreadable in the first accepted scan, when _soundBaseline is false (for example, Zenith starts with 'Mute clients when they appear' already saved on and the first scan hits a transient InvalidOperationException or Win32Exception). That client never enters the seen set. On the next readable scan it counts as a new arrival, so a client that was already running gets muted. The fixer noted this gap.
O-C6-1.proposedFix: While not watching, including the baseline scan, keep a bounded set (at most 128) of unreadable PIDs. When that PID's instance first reads cleanly, add its key to the seen set without making it an arrival. Add a presentation test: the first scan cannot read client 2, later scans read it, and client 2 is never muted.

O-C6-2.problem: If a Mute or Unmute click is waiting on an arrival operation, and that operation reaches a final result (for example, it mutes the new client), the arrival's rows and its 'N of M new clients muted as they appeared' status are dropped. O-C6-3.kind: minor finding from round 3's independent lane review (verify it first; the reviewer can be wrong)
O-C6-3.title: The fixer confirmed this test also passes without the fix
O-C6-3.problem: The fixer confirmed this test also passes without the fix. It never checks that the waiting arrival keeps its original first-seen time. A regression that drops the arrival and re-adds it with a new time after an unreadable scan would still pass, and in that regression a periodically unreadable client could be retried past the 2-minute ArrivalMuteWindow.
O-C6-3.proposedFix: Make arrival time controllable: inject a TimeProvider instead of calling DateTimeOffset.UtcNow in ObserveClientSoundArrivals and PublishArrivalSound. Then assert that a NoAudioSession retry after an unreadable scan becomes final once the original first-seen time is more than ArrivalMuteWindow old.

O-C10-2.kind: minor finding from round 3's independent lane review (verify it first; the reviewer can be wrong)
O-C10-2.title: InternalsVisibleTo("Zenith.MacroHost.Execution") was added only so the runner can reach StopAsync(string)
O-C10-2.problem: InternalsVisibleTo("Zenith.MacroHost.Execution") was added only so the runner can reach StopAsync(string). Before this the assembly exposed no internals to anyone. It now exposes the input owner's whole internal surface to the execution layer: the Sync lock object, the Lane semaphore, the raw ITargetedInputTransport, the TargetedInputRun constructor, and RequestStopLocked/ReleaseLocked/TrackLocked, which assume the caller already holds Sync. Nothing misuses them today. But the execution assembly could now send input around the coordinator's admission and ownership checks (Rule 4 single input pipeline, Rule 13) or call *Locked methods without the lock.
O-C10-2.proposedFix: Remove the InternalsVisibleTo. Add a narrow public API instead, for example a public StopAsync(TargetedInputStopReason) with a closed enum (Completed, RuntimeLimit, AfterFailure, CompanionStopped, RunnerClosed, NotStarted), with the texts mapped inside Zenith.Automation.Input.

O-C10-3.kind: minor finding from round 3's independent lane review (verify it first; the reviewer can be wrong)
O-C10-3.title: I confirmed the fixer's side note
O-C10-3.location: src/Zenith.MacroHost.Execution/TargetedMacroPlayer.cs:131-133 (pre-existing; found by the N-B9-4 fixer, not recorded)
O-C10-3.problem: I confirmed the fixer's side note. When the runtime cap's token cancels a key send in progress, TargetedInputRun.DispatchAsync stops the input itself ('Input batch cancelled; ...') and returns Cancelled with run state Stopping. The player continues only for Pausing, Paused, Resuming or Clearing, so it throws Failure(), sets Rejected, and the run finalizes as Faulted/InputRejected instead of Stopped/RuntimeLimit. The new runtime-limit test sidesteps this with a delay-only macro. No app constructs CompanionMacroOperations yet, so no user sees this today. The item is not in QUALITY_STATUS.md.
O-C10-3.proposedFix: Open a work item. Treat a Cancelled dispatch caused by the run's own runtime cap (effectiveCt) as a stop, not a rejection, and add a test that hits the cap during a key send.

O-C10-5.title: Test-harness hygiene (Rule 12)
O-C10-5.problem: Test-harness hygiene (Rule 12).
